user.title: SolarEdge application credentials
user.description:
Create a **Site Access** application in the [SolarEdge developer console]({console}) with the scopes SITE_DATA and DEVICE_DATA and enter the Client ID and Client Secret here.

**Redirect URL** - add exactly the same address under *Allowed Redirect URL(s)* of the application:
- `{callback}` - Home Assistant catches the redirect itself (needs an HTTPS address of this Home Assistant that your browser can open, e.g. your external URL), or
- `http://localhost/callback` - you paste the address from the browser by hand.

data.redirect_uri: Redirect URL registered in the console

authorize.title: Approve access
authorize.description:
1. [Open the SolarEdge consent page]({url}), sign in with your mySolarEdge account and click **Approve**.
2. The browser then opens `{redirect}?code=...&site_id=...` and shows a connection error - that is expected.
3. Copy the **whole address** from the browser's address bar and paste it below. The code is valid only for a short time.

data.redirect_url: Address from the browser's address bar

reauth_confirm.title: Approve access again
reauth_confirm.description:
SolarEdge rejected the stored token (it expires after 30 days without use or when the 24-month consent ends).

1. [Open the SolarEdge consent page]({url}) and click **Approve**.
2. Paste the whole address the browser lands on (`{redirect}?code=...`).

data.redirect_url: Address from the browser's address bar

billing.title: Credit cycle start day
billing.description:
SolarEdge does not report the billing cycle through the API, so the integration needs it to count credits correctly.

Open the [developer portal Dashboard]({dashboard}) and look at **Subscription start date**: enter its day of the month (for example 16 for 16.10.2026). It is usually the day you created your developer account. The credits reset on that day every month.

data.billing_day: Day of month the credits reset

migrate.title: Take over the built-in SolarEdge sensors

data.migrate: Take over these sensors and their history

external.title: Approve access at SolarEdge
external.description: Sign in with your mySolarEdge account in the window that opens and click **Approve**. Home Assistant receives the answer by itself; then come back here.

reauth_redirect.title: Re-authorize SolarEdge
reauth_redirect.description:
SolarEdge needs your approval again (the token expired after 30 days without use, or the 24-month consent ended).

Confirm the **Redirect URL**. It must be listed under *Allowed Redirect URL(s)* in your SolarEdge application. Suggested: `{callback}` (Home Assistant receives the answer by itself); `http://localhost/callback` means pasting the address by hand.

reconfigure.title: Change SolarEdge application settings
reconfigure.description:
Change the Client ID, Client Secret or the **Redirect URL** (it must be listed under *Allowed Redirect URL(s)* in the [SolarEdge developer console]({console})). Suggested: `{callback}`.

After saving you approve access again; history, sensors and the credit counter stay.

error.invalid_redirect: No authorization code found in the pasted text.
error.site_id_missing: The address has no site_id; enter the Site ID shown on the consent page.
error.invalid_code: SolarEdge rejected the code (expired, already used, or the Client Secret / redirect URL do not match). Open the consent page again.
error.no_site_access: These credentials cannot read this site.

abort.wrong_site: You approved a different site than the one configured.

init.title: Polling and sensors
init.description:
Credits used this cycle: **{used} / {limit}**. Each daytime poll costs **{calls_per_poll}** credit(s), plus about **{daily_fixed}** credit(s) a day for daily data.

With the current settings: fixed mode polls every **{fixed} min**, adaptive mode would poll every **{adaptive} min** right now. Projected use at the end of the cycle: **{projected}**.

The more groups you enable, the less often the integration can poll within the same limit.

data.totals: Energy this month / this year / lifetime (1 credit a day)
data.overview: Consumption, import, export, self-consumption - sites with a meter only (+1 credit per poll)
data.monthly_credits: Monthly credit limit of your plan
data.billing_day: Day of month the credit cycle starts (see the developer portal Dashboard)

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.description:
With these settings:

- fixed mode: a poll every **{fixed} min** (sized for the longest day of the year)
- adaptive mode: a poll every **{adaptive} min** right now
- one poll costs **{calls_per_poll}** credit(s); daily data about **{daily_fixed}**
- credits used: **{used} / {limit}**, projected at the end of the cycle: **{projected}**

Submit to save.

options.fixed: Fixed - one interval all year, sized for the longest day
options.adaptive: Adaptive - spread the remaining credits over the remaining daylight

auth_failed.message: SolarEdge rejected the token; re-authorize the integration.

credits_exhausted.message: The monthly API credits are used up; polling resumes when the cycle resets.

credits_exhausted.title: SolarEdge API credits used up
credits_exhausted.description: SolarEdge refused further calls this month. Polling resumes on {reset}. Consider fewer sensor groups or a larger reserve in the integration options.

consent_expiring.title: SolarEdge consent expires soon
consent_expiring.description: The 24-month Site Access consent ends on {date}. Re-authorize the integration (Settings > Devices & services > SolarEdge Monitoring API v2 > Reconfigure / Re-authenticate) before then.

core_migrated.title: SolarEdge sensors taken over
core_migrated.description:
These sensors now belong to SolarEdge Monitoring API v2 and keep their history: {entities}.

The built-in SolarEdge integration was disabled. Once everything looks right you can delete it (Settings > Devices & services). If Repairs offers to delete statistics of the old sensors, do not.

init.title: Credit cycle start day
init.description:
The integration assumed the credits reset on day **{day}** (the day it was added). SolarEdge does not report the real day through the API.

Open the [developer portal Dashboard]({dashboard}), check **Subscription start date** and enter its day of the month. It is usually the day you created your developer account.
